title: Observability memory landscape and dashboard tiling notes
body:
Context and intent:

This is a working note for a small sprint (2 weeks) focused on two adjacent problems we keep hitting during rollouts: 1) dashboard density + tile hygiene when operators need a single-pane incident view, and 2) memory-related telemetry across model sidecars and host runtimes (KV cache pressure, prefix warmth, eviction churn). The goal is to produce a lightweight spec + checklist that the oncall team and a handful of PM/Eng can iterate on quickly.

Why this matters now:
- Recent canary rolled back because the operator dashboard surface didn’t show a joint signal (cache evictions + tail latency) in one glance (see JIRA-OBS-741).
- Customers (enterprise Dedicated) flagged intermittent 503s that correlate poorly with CPU but strongly with x-kvcache-eviction spikes.
- We are planning a quantized model rollout next quarter; memory behavior and dashboard clarity need to be stable before broad rollout.

Assumptions and constraints:
- We must keep query cost low: sampling + aggregation choices should avoid high-cardinality payloads by default.
- Dashboard should support a rapid 3-metric triage lane (at-a-glance) and an extended lane for deeper drilldowns.
- Tracing changes must preserve PII/PHI redaction rules (see security-and-compliance on key redaction patterns).

Proposal summary (high level):
1) A compact incident tile set (3 tiles) per operator persona: "Memory heat", "Latency tail", "Error surface". Each tile is a derived rollup to reduce noise.
2) A fallback tracing sampling mode for memory spikes that increases span retention for affected sessions only (session-linked adaptive sampling).
3) A lightweight metric taxonomy for memory signals (three derived metrics + raw counters kept behind a permission flag).

Metric definitions (candidate list, keep names short):
- mem.kv_eviction_rate_p95: "p95 eviction ops per min per instance" (derived, window=5m)
- mem.kv_warmth_index: "fraction of requests served from prefix cache within TTL" (0..1)
- mem.host_rss_percentile_99: "host RSS (MB) p99 normalized by instance flavor memory"
- mem.prefetch_miss_rate: "prefetch attempts that failed to find prefixes in local cache (1m rate)"
- request.ttftt_p99: "time-to-first-token tail p99" (keep separate from TTFB; measured end-to-end)
- request.kv_miss_tail_latency_p95: "p95 latency for requests that experienced a kv miss on first token"
- system.eviction_churn_index: "normalized churn score combining eviction_count and re-pop rate (heuristic 0..100)"

Notes on derivation and retention:
- Derived metrics (eviction_rate_p95, warmth_index, churn_index) are computed in our metrics pipeline (ingest -> transform layer). Keep raw eviction_count and raw prefix_hit_count but only at 1m granularity and 7d retention by default.
- Tail percentiles (p95/p99) should use HDR histograms for efficient rollups.
- For Dedicated/Private customers we may expose 30d retention via config but default is 7d to cap PromQL cost.

Tracing: sampling and annotation plan:
- Default tracing sampling stays low (1%) for production traffic across fleets.
- Introduce "memory-spike ad-hoc sampling" that flips to 50% for sessions where mem.kv_eviction_rate_p95 > threshold (configurable). Implementation idea: lightweight pre-filter hook on ingestion that attaches a small session flag and routes spans for those sessions to higher retention.
- Add span annotations: kv.op=(hit|miss|evict|prefetch), kv.size_mb, kv.ttl_ms, model.seq_len_hint. Keep these as short tags to reduce cardinality.
- Traces must attach a single stable session_id across microcalls and model sidecars to stitch; we already emit session_id for requests but verify across the model sidecar boundary (Samira to validate artifact in PR 209).

Dashboard tiling and UX patterns (operator lanes):
- Primary compact tile group (single-row compact form):
  * Memory heat (sparkline of mem.kv_warmth_index with p95 overlay)
  * Latency tail (request.ttftt_p99)
  * Error surface (5m error rate + top error kinds stacked)
- Secondary expandable lane (accordion) per tile for drilldown: e.g., Memory heat expands to show eviction_rate_p95, prefetch_miss_rate, and a small histogram of kv.op counts.
- Tile sizing rules: compact group should be readable on a widescreen 1440p window without vertical scroll. Aim for 3 tiles per full-width row.
- Dashboard pagination: add a "focused session" quick filter to pin a session_id and auto-aggregate traces & logs for that session across sidecars.

Operational checklist for rollout (quick wins and blockers):
- Quick wins:
  1) Add mem.kv_eviction_rate_p95 to existing operator microdash (Ava).
  2) Create a simple alert for eviction_rate_p95 > X sustained 5m AND ttftt_p99 > Y (team to pick thresholds).
  3) Add an annotation that shows the last config rollout ID on chart hover.
- Blockers / questions:
  * Where will the adaptive tracing spool be stored? Need SRE input on retention cost (Marcus).
  * How to safely aggregate kv.tag values: we must avoid unbounded tag sets from user-provided keys. Decide to allow kv.op but never kv.key.
  * Do we need to expose raw prefix lists for debugging? Prefer behind a permission gate.

Cost & sampling tradeoffs (engineering constraints):
- Traces are the most expensive signal. The adaptive sampling approach attempts to keep noise low by only increasing sampling when memory signals indicate risk. However, we must cap budget per-cluster (e.g., 10k extra spans/day/cluster). Marcus to propose per-cluster caps.
- Metric rollups should be computed in the transform layer to avoid high-cardinality time series stored for long periods. Use rollups to 1m/5m buckets.

Implementation plan and owners (first sprint):
- Week 1 (owners: Ava + Samira):
  * Add derived metric mem.kv_eviction_rate_p95, mem.kv_warmth_index to metrics pipeline, verify ingestion for one canary host.
  * Add compact tile placeholder in "operator microdash" (wireframe only).
- Week 2 (owners: Marcus + Riley):
  * Implement adaptive tracing flag hook in trace-ingest (prototype, route higher retention spans to special storage).
  * Implement dashboard accordion behavior and focused session filter.

Open experiments and hypothesis logging (for later backfilling):
- Hypothesis A: Most visible operator incidents are caused by sudden prefetch_miss_rate jumps that lead to eviction cascades; if we can correlate 3-minute jump in prefetch_miss_rate with cache churn we can trigger preemptive throttling.
- Hypothesis B: Exposing a single "warmth index" as a compact visual reduces mean time to detect by 30% for oncall. Will instrument MTTR in next sprint.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Samira: confirm PR 209 instrumentation adds model.seq_len_hint to spans without leaking model inputs.
- Ava: pick provisional thresholds and add to JIRA-OBS-741 for discussion with oncall.
- Marcus: calculate cost model for adaptive tracing and propose a default per-cluster cap by 2026-02-05.

Appendix: quick links and references:
- Related docs: serving-runtime/serving-runtime-observability-integration-guidelines-metric-deck.json (observability integration checklist)
- Security notes: see security-and-compliance/trace-privacy-redaction-notes (ensure session_id cannot be correlated to PHI)
- Slack threads: #ops-observability memory-eviction-jan2026 (search in Slack)

This is intentionally concise and opinionated. The aim is to iterate fast: implement the three-tile compact view + metric derivations and confirm whether adaptive tracing yields useful signal before broadening retention or exposing more raw counters.

Unresolved decisions (to close by sprint planning):
- Finalize thresholds (eviction_rate, ttftt) and alert severity mapping.
- Confirm storage plan for higher-retention traces and budget allocation.
- Decide on permission gating UI for raw prefix lists."
